mitdb.name: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
mitdb.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
mitdb.desc: 48 half-hour two-lead ambulatory recordings (Beth Israel Hospital, 1975–1979) with beat-by-beat and rhythm annotations by cardiologists.
mitdb.cite: Moody GB, Mark RG. IEEE Eng Med Biol 2001;20(3):45–50. Goldberger AL et al. PhysioNet. Circulation 2000;101:e215–e220.

georgia.name: Georgia 12-lead ECG Challenge Database (Emory University), PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021
georgia.desc: 12-lead, 10-second ECGs from patients in the south-eastern United States, labelled with SNOMED CT diagnoses. Sample records as redistributed by the torch_ecg project.
georgia.cite: Reyna MA et al. Computing in Cardiology 2021;48. Perez Alday EA et al. Physiol Meas 2020;41:124003.

ludb.name: Lobachevsky University Electrocardiography Database v1.0.1
ludb.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
ludb.desc: 200 twelve-lead, 10-second ECGs (500 Hz) from Nizhny Novgorod City Hospital No 5, with rhythm and diagnosis labels and wave boundaries marked by cardiologists. Includes acute STEMI, ischaemia, scar, AV block, pacing and AF.
ludb.cite: Kalyakulina AI et al. LUDB: a new open-access validation tool for electrocardiogram delineation algorithms. IEEE Access 2020;8:186181–90.

ptbxl.name: PTB-XL, a large publicly available electrocardiography dataset v1.0.x
ptbxl.desc: 21,799 twelve-lead, 10-second ECGs from 18,869 patients (Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Berlin), annotated with SCP-ECG statements by up to two cardiologists. Sample records as redistributed in open-source GitHub projects.
ptbxl.cite: Wagner P et al. PTB-XL, a large publicly available electrocardiography dataset. Sci Data 2020;7:154.

cpsc.name: China Physiological Signal Challenge 2018 (via PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2020/2021)
cpsc.desc: Twelve-lead ECGs (6–60 s, 500 Hz) from 11 Chinese hospitals, SNOMED CT labels. First 10 s shown.
cpsc.cite: Liu F et al. J Med Imaging Health Inform 2018;8:1368–73. Reyna MA et al. Computing in Cardiology 2021;48.

chapman.name: Chapman University & Shaoxing People’s Hospital 12-lead ECG database (via PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021)
chapman.desc: Ten-second, 500 Hz twelve-lead ECGs with SNOMED CT rhythm and morphology labels.
chapman.cite: Zheng J et al. A 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia research covering more than 10,000 patients. Sci Data 2020;7:48. Reyna MA et al. CinC 2021;48.

cinc17.name: AF Classification from a Short Single Lead ECG Recording: PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2017
cinc17.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
cinc17.desc: Single-lead 9–60 s recordings from an AliveCor handheld device, labelled normal, AF, other rhythm or noisy.
cinc17.cite: Clifford GD et al. AF classification from a short single lead ECG recording. Computing in Cardiology 2017;44.

ptbdb.name: PTB Diagnostic ECG Database
ptbdb.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
ptbdb.desc: 549 high-resolution 15-lead recordings (1 kHz) from 290 people at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Berlin, with clinical summaries: acute and old myocardial infarction (with infarction and ECG dates), bundle branch block, cardiomyopathy, dysrhythmia, hypertrophy, valve disease, myocarditis and healthy controls. The 12 standard leads are shown, 10 s per recording.
ptbdb.cite: Bousseljot R, Kreiseler D, Schnabel A. Biomed Tech 1995;40(S1):317. Goldberger AL et al. Circulation 2000;101:e215–e220.

incart.name: St Petersburg INCART 12-lead Arrhythmia Database
incart.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
incart.desc: 75 half-hour 12-lead Holter-style recordings (257 Hz) from 32 patients with coronary artery disease and arrhythmias, with beat and rhythm annotations. Tihonenko V et al., PhysioNet 2008. Retrieved via github.com/miguelaltuve/multichannelQRSdetector.

afdb.name: MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database
afdb.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
afdb.desc: 25 ten-hour two-lead ambulatory recordings (250 Hz) of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, with rhythm annotations. Moody GB, Mark RG, Computers in Cardiology 1983. Retrieved via github.com/TenzinDhonyoe/SVM_data_processing_for_atrial_fibrillation_detection.

ltafdb.name: Long Term AF Database
ltafdb.lic: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
ltafdb.desc: 84 two-lead 24-hour ambulatory recordings (128 Hz) of paroxysmal or sustained AF, with beat and rhythm annotations. Petrutiu S et al., Europace 2007. Retrieved via github.com/TenzinDhonyoe/SVM_data_processing_for_atrial_fibrillation_detection.
